Report_ID: Cure ratio (discharged from OTP as cured)
Title: The effectiveness of treatment for Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) delivered by community health workers compared to a traditional facility based model
Author: Alvarez Morán et al.
Comment: Table 6 was used as the pre-identified primary Results location. Its adjusted reported RR of 1.89 (95% CI 1.09–3.27) is numerically inconsistent with the displayed cure proportions/counts and with the abstract's RR of 1.07 (95% CI 1.01–1.13); no correction was invented. The Results narrative gives the control percentage as 88.6%, whereas Table 6 gives 88.2%; the table value accompanies the extracted counts. Denominators are children discharged from OTP (617 and 212), not all admitted children (699 and 235), so this is not clearly intention-to-treat. The intervention area used mixed delivery: 79% of admissions occurred through CHWs and 21% at health facilities. Geographic/facility clustering is possible, but no ICC, average cluster size, or explicitly cluster-adjusted RR is reported; therefore the requested design-effect adjustment cannot be calculated from the paper. An assumed ICC of 0.02 (or sensitivity ICC 0.05) alone is insufficient without an average cluster size.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention group: outpatient SAM treatment delivered by Community Health Workers and health facilities') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Child nutrition; treatment of severe acute malnutrition
Study Environment: Community Health Workers and outpatient health centres in Kita district
Topic of Content: Treatment of uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition
Participant type: Children aged 6–59 months with severe acute malnutrition
Recruitment source: Children admitted to outpatient SAM treatment in intervention and control areas
Outcome measurement: Cured according to national CMAM protocol: Weight-for-Height Z score ≥ −1.5 and absence of nutritional oedema during 14 days, or MUAC >125 mm and absence of nutritional oedema during 14 days.
Outcome variable: Cure ratio (discharged from OTP as cured)
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher recovery with lay health workers; observed cure proportion favors the intervention arm

Report_ID: Cure from severe acute malnutrition (MUAC ≥ 12.5 cm)
Title: Effectiveness of screening and treatment of children with severe acute malnutrition by community health workers in Simiyu region, Tanzania: a quasi-experimental pilot study
Author: Wilunda et al.
Comment: The extracted RR is the adjusted multiple-imputation intention-to-treat estimate and is oriented as CHW intervention versus facility control. The control cure count of 116 is the paper's imputed count; six control outcomes were originally missing. Treatment was geographically organized in three intervention and three control wards, but the paper reports no ICC and does not state that this RR/CI was cluster-adjusted. Per the synthesis plan, clustering would therefore require an assumed ICC of 0.02 for the primary analysis and 0.05 for sensitivity analysis; the paper does not provide a cluster-adjusted estimate or an explicit average cluster size for this purpose.
Design Type: Parallel two-arm non-inferiority quasi-experimental pilot study
Study Environment: Community/home treatment in Bariadi intervention wards versus facility-based outpatient therapeutic care in Maswa control wards, Simiyu Region
Medium: Home-based care versus health-facility outpatient care
Topic of Content: Treatment of uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition with ready-to-use therapeutic food
interaction_type: Weekly CHW home follow-up versus follow-up by professional health workers through outpatient therapeutic care clinics
Participant type: Children aged 6–59 months with uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition
Recruitment source: Community recruitment by CHWs in intervention wards and recruitment by formal health workers in health facilities in control wards
Outcome measurement: Cure from SAM defined as MUAC ≥ 12.5 cm
Outcome variable: Cure from severe acute malnutrition (MUAC ≥ 12.5 cm)
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher recovery with lay health workers; observed recovery favors the CHW arm

Title: Effectiveness and Coverage of Treatment for Severe Acute Malnutrition Delivered by Community Health Workers in the Guidimakha Region, Mauritania
Author: Charle-Cuéllar et al.
Comment: The paper reports a crude Cox-model hazard ratio, not a risk ratio. For the planned recovery RR, use the reported cure counts among children with known outcomes: CHWs 60/78 versus health staff 319/418. The paper reports unknown outcomes for 28 CHW-treated and 94 health-facility-treated children, so these are complete-case rather than intention-to-treat denominators. The comparison is nonrandomized and baseline MUAC severity differed by provider. No cluster adjustment or ICC is reported; this is not described as a cluster-randomized design.
Study Environment: Community and outpatient health-facility settings in a rural agro-pastoral region
Topic of Content: Treatment of uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition
interaction_type: Clinical treatment delivered by community health workers or professional health staff
Participant type: Children aged 6–59 months with uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition
Recruitment source: Children presenting to or detected for treatment at health facilities or CHW sites, including community screening, volunteers, and mobile clinics
Outcome measurement: Discharged as cured, defined as absence of oedema and WHZ equal to or greater than 1.5 or/and MUAC >125 mm during two consecutive weeks
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher recovery with lay health workers; observed cure proportions are nearly equal and slightly favor CHWs

Title: A large-scale operational study of home-based therapy with ready-to-use therapeutic food in childhood malnutrition in Malawi
Author: Zachary Linneman, Danielle Matilsky, MacDonald Ndekha, Micah J. Manary, Ken Maleta, and Mark J. Manary
Comment: The lay-health-worker arm combines two explicitly reported staffing strata: 670/738 plus 264/292, yielding 934/1030. The study was non-randomized and treatment was clustered within centres. No ICC or cluster-adjusted RR/CI was reported; under the synthesis plan, variance should therefore be adjusted using an assumed ICC of 0.02 in the primary analysis and 0.05 in sensitivity analysis. Average cluster size for the combined two-arm comparison is not explicitly reported and should not be guessed. The enrolled age range was 6–60 months, one month wider than the target range of 6–59 months. The paper reports no provider-specific recovery comparison for moderately malnourished children.
Design Type: Non-randomized multicentre operational cohort study with centre-level staffing models
domain: Treatment of childhood severe acute malnutrition
Study Environment: 12 rural treatment centres in southern Malawi
Medium: In-person home-based RUTF treatment with fortnightly clinic follow-up
Topic of Content: Treatment of severe childhood malnutrition with ready-to-use therapeutic food
interaction_type: Treatment administered by medical professionals or community health aids
Participant type: Children aged 6–60 months with severe malnutrition and a good appetite
Recruitment source: Children presenting to 12 centres in southern Malawi from May 2005 to May 2006
Outcome measurement: Recovered if oedema resolved and final weight-for-height was >85% of ideal weight-for-height
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher recovery with lay health workers; observed recovery favors community health aids

Title: Impact of Integration of Severe Acute Malnutrition Treatment in Primary Health Care Provided by Community Health Workers in Rural Niger
Author: Dougnon et al.
Comment: The paper reports an admission-criteria-adjusted Cox hazard ratio, not a risk ratio, for cure. For the planned meta-analysis, calculate the lay-worker-versus-professional RR from the extracted raw counts (CHWs 655/782; health staff 863/1181); no computed RR is entered here because the anti-hallucination instruction restricts numeric fields to values stated verbatim. The reported p value is a threshold (<0.001), so p_value is left null rather than recording 0.001 as an exact value. No ICC is reported. Although treatment was delivered within provider/facility settings, the paper does not explicitly provide the average cluster size needed for the prespecified design-effect correction; clustering assumptions must therefore be handled at synthesis stage.
domain: Treatment of uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition in children
Study Environment: Rural intervention commune; community health huts and health facilities
Participant type: Children aged 6–59 months with uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition
Recruitment source: Children attending health facilities or community health worker huts from June 2018 to March 2019
Outcome measurement: Recovery was defined as no edema for 14 days and WHZ ≥ −2 z score and/or MUAC ≥ 125 mm (depending on admission criterion) during two consecutive follow-up visits
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher recovery with lay health workers; observed cure proportion favors CHWs
